thread:
Anna W: Quick sync — Customer Bravo pushed back on our default Dedicated commitment terms. They want a hard SLA: 99.95% P99 latency for text-generation routes during their peak window (US-EAST business hours).

Rahul S: Noted. Do we have telemetry to prove we can hit 99.95% at their expected QPS?

capacity-bot: Recent sim run (2026-02-18): avg P99=220ms at 1200 qps with 2x warm pool. 95th percentile of runs meet 99.9% target under synthetic load.

Kim T: Two quick things: (1) SLA target implies sizing + autoscale constraints; (2) acceptance criteria must include fallback behavior if warm pool exhausted.

Anna W: Proposal: define PRD acceptance as:
- SLA: 99.95% P99 latency over 1h rolling window during committed peak.
- Throughput sizing: per-customer reserved pool baseline = ceil(peak_qps / per-GPU-max-qps) + burst buffer (20%).
- Autoscale policy: warm pool target, cold-start cap, scale-up latency budget.
- Canary/rollback: automatic fallback to compatible smaller model or lower concurrency route on breach.

Rahul S: Suggested concrete numbers for PRD:
- per-GPU sustained throughput = 300 qps (fp16, 8k context) as baseline.
- warm pool = 2 GPUs per 600 qps committed.
- burst buffer = +20% for 5m rolling windows.
- cold-start cap = allow 10% calls to queue with 5s max wait before rejecting.

Jordan P: Edge cases to capture in PRD:
- Region failover: if primary region capacity exhausted, auto-failover must not violate data residency for regulated customers.
- Long-tail inputs: extremely long sequences (>=16k tokens) should be routed to a coldpath with different SLA and pricing.
- Multi-customer noisy neighbor: ensure isolation by capping per-customer batch sizes and KV cache partitioning.

Kim T: Acceptance test checklist (to include in PRD):
1) Load test at committed qps for 4hrs with synthetic and recorded production traces. P99 measured <= SLA.
2) Induce warm-pool drain: simulate 50% of warm GPUs offline, validate graceful degradation for others and canary fallback.
3) Autoscale hysteresis test: repeated spikes every 30s to ensure no oscillation.
4) Canary rollback path triggered and validated.

Anna W: Scope negotiation: recommend shipping MVP for commitments with these limits (no per-tenant dynamic pricing, no per-route custom SLAs). Move per-tenant SLAs & on-prem residency to v2.

Rahul S: Risk note: hitting 99.95 P99 may require tighter admission control + more conservative batching. That increases cost. Need a pricing addendum.

Jordan P: Ops runbook bits: include a clear runbook step:
- "If SLA breach detected for >10m: shift traffic to fallback model, notify oncall, increase warm pool if capacity available, and open incident with root cause labeling (warm-pool/cold-start/noisy-neighbor)."

Anna W: Action items:
- Rahul: update PRD with concrete numbers above, include cost impact section. (due EOD Tue)
- Kim: write acceptance test matrix + test harness requirements. (due Thu)
- Jordan: draft runbook steps and map to existing oncall playbooks. (due Thu)
- Ops: queue load tests for next sprint (tag: perf/dedicated).

Rahul S: +1. I'll also add a short section on canary funnel and metrics to watch: p50/p95/p99, cold-start rate, queueing fraction, warm-pool utilization.

Kim T: :thumbsup: Sounds good. One more ask from legal: include data retention & KMS behavior during failover — I'll ping security to add a short paragraph.

Anna W: Thanks team. We'll use this as the nucleus for the PRD. Keeping MVP narrow will help get commitments live without blocking on per-tenant pricing.

capacity-bot: PRD skeleton created: /docs/prd/dedicated-commitments-1768130000.md (draft).

Anna W: I'll upload the draft this afternoon and @product-review for a quick pass.

Jordan P: FYI I scheduled a 30m sync for tomorrow 10:30 to walk the acceptance criteria.

Rahul S: I'll bring perf numbers and two candidate autoscale configs.

Kim T: meeting invite accepted.

Anna W: End.
